newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian anti-tobacco bill to be introduced Monday.
newsitem.headline: Canadian anti-tobacco bill to be introduced Monday.

text.p: Canadian Health Minister David Dingwall said on Friday he planned to introduce his new anti-tobacco legislation on Monday.
"I hope to give notice later this afternoon of the tabling of the bill on Monday," Dingwall told Parliament a day after unveiling the main points of the plan.
The government package will ban tobacco advertisements on radio, television or billboards; prohibit vending machine sales; and restrict the use of brand names in sponsoring sporting and other events.
The three major players in the Canadian tobacco market are:
- Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd, which controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc of Britain.
- Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, owned 60 percent by Rothmans International, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
- RJR MacDonald, wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
